idea: baseline: average of the last 7 days
Regress load on weekday plus heating/cooling degree days
Fit log load instead of raw load, then exponentiate
Add yesterday's heating/cooling degrees as extra regression features
Shift heating/cooling thresholds to 18C and 22C

Add yearly seasonal sine/cosine terms to the regression

lesson: agent's scorer said 3.036 → 3.186; code lost, not re-measured

idea: Add quadratic heating/cooling degree terms to regression
lesson: Extra flexibility (weekend-temperature interactions, quadratic degree terms) overfits and hurts; the simple linear model is hard to beat.

idea: Add half the last-28-day mean residual as level correction
lesson: A slowly moving 28-day mean residual gives a small gain (3.036 to 2.995) that clears practice, but it's probably too small for the judge's bar.

idea: Exponentially time-weighted regression fit favoring recent days
lesson: Recency weighting doesn't help (half-life 120d worse, 300d tied); the stable linear fit is already near the noise floor.

idea: Use average of today's and yesterday's temperature forecast in regression
lesson: Smoothing temperature over two days gives no gain (3.036 to 3.038); residuals look like noise around the linear fit.

idea: Add heating/cooling degrees of prior 3-day mean temperature
lesson: Lagged multi-day temperature carries real signal (3.036 to 2.890, 99.9% wins), though a similar yesterday-only idea was previously thrown away at the judge.

idea: Blend today's temperature with prior 3-day mean into one effective temperature
lesson: Replacing today's temperature with a blend of it and prior days hurts or ties; lagged temperature only helps as a separate added feature, and that was already thrown away.

idea: Grid-search heating/cooling thresholds in fit()
lesson: Choosing thresholds by in-sample SSE overfits (3.036 to 3.187); the fixed 17C/21C thresholds generalize better.

idea: Add recent 7/14-day mean residual as level correction
lesson: Short-window residual level corrections (7 or 14 days) give no gain over the plain regression, so the remaining error looks like day-to-day noise.

idea: Add one lagged 5-day mean temperature extremity feature to regression
lesson: A single combined heating/cooling extremity term on the prior 5-day mean temperature gives a clear practice gain (3.036 to 2.866) with only one extra parameter.

idea: Add |prior 7-day mean temp − 19C| feature to regression
lesson: Residuals show no weekday, holiday or autocorrelation signal, and the only gain is lagged temperature, a near-copy of ideas the judge already threw away.

idea: Add day-over-day forecast temperature change feature
lesson: Today-minus-yesterday temperature change adds no signal (3.036 to 3.059); only multi-day lagged temperature level has helped.

idea: Pool Mon–Fri into one day dummy; keep Sat and Sun separate
lesson: Fewer day dummies cut noise and win 99.79% of practice reshuffles, but the gain is small (3.036 to 2.989) against the judge's 99.5% bar.

idea: Combine pooled weekdays with prior 5-day temperature extremity feature
lesson: Merging two separately small gains (pooled weekday dummies, lagged temperature) gives 3.036 to 2.847, a larger gain than either alone.

idea: Pooled weekdays plus exponentially weighted prior-temperature extremity feature
lesson: An exponentially weighted history of past temperatures works as a lagged feature (3.036 to 2.838), but it's close to earlier lagged-temperature ideas that the judge threw away.

idea: Huber-weighted robust regression instead of least squares
lesson: Downweighting outlier days hurts (3.036 to 3.064); residuals are near-Gaussian noise, so robust fitting adds nothing.

idea: Add linear time trend feature to regression
lesson: A linear trend adds nothing (3.036 to 3.043); there's no sign of load growth beyond the temperature and weekday effects.

idea: Pooled weekdays plus separate lagged 5-day heating/cooling degree features
lesson: Lagged-temperature variants all land near 2.85-2.88 and win practice, but they are near-copies of ideas the judge already threw away, so I'm not submitting.

idea: Pooled weekdays plus |prior 14-day mean temp − 19C| feature
lesson: A 14-day lagged temperature feature again lands near 2.88, the same gain as the earlier lagged-temperature ideas the judge threw away, so it adds no new information.

idea: Pooled weekdays, Saturday, and Sunday-or-US-federal-holiday dummies
lesson: Treating US federal holidays like Sundays hurts (3.036 to 3.230); the data shows no holiday effect, so the remaining error is noise.

idea: Single V-shaped |temp − 19C| term replacing heating/cooling degrees
lesson: Removing the dead band between heating and cooling hurts (3.036 to 3.131); residuals show no day-of-month, month or autocorrelation signal, so only the noise floor remains.

idea: Lower heating/cooling thresholds to 15C and 20C
lesson: Moving the thresholds to 15C/20C clearly hurts (3.036 to 3.410); the 17C/21C thresholds are better, and the residuals look like noise.

idea: Add prior-3-day max/min temperature extremes as heat/cold features, pooled weekdays
lesson: Prior-3-day temperature extremes give only a small gain (3.036 to 2.945), weaker than earlier lagged-mean features, and likely too small for the judge's bar.

idea: Pooled weekdays, 5-day lagged temperature extremity, plus half the 28-day residual level
lesson: Stacking small gains reaches only 2.867, no better than the thrown-away idea 20 (2.847), so lagged-temperature variants have saturated and I'm not submitting.

idea: Shift heating/cooling thresholds to 16C and 22C
lesson: Widening the dead band to 16C/22C helps on practice (3.036 to 2.959, 97.55% wins), but the gain is small and probably short of the judge's 99.64% bar. Moving only one threshold gains much less.

idea: Pooled Mon–Fri dummy plus 16C/22C heating/cooling thresholds
lesson: Combining two small gains (pooled weekdays, wider dead band) gives 3.036 to 2.904, but still smaller than the lagged-temperature ideas.

idea: Pooled weekdays, 16/22C thresholds, plus 5-day lagged temperature extremity
lesson: Stacking three individually small gains (pooled weekdays, wider dead band, lagged temperature) reached 2.785, a bigger gain than any pair tried earlier.
